title: The far side, from the inside

data.source: Cut locus and injectivity radius (Riemannian geometry); Bhattacharyya angle (1943); Bures metric and Uhlmann fidelity; the mean-chord argument of colloquy/mathematical.md. Numerical check on the worked circle of Phoenix_Egg/CORE/MATHEMATICS.md, the lens's generic circle and 40 more random circles, seeded.

prediction: On R1's circle and a generic circle the ambient distance across a half-turn is always below a (F1); some half-turn has straight chord at most 2a/pi (F2); R1's circle is a trine measurement of a qubit of radius 0.6 (F3); and for a qubit the ratio is 2 arcsin(r)/(pi r), reaching 1 only for pure states (F4).
baseline: The cut locus of Riemannian geometry, the Bhattacharyya angle and the Bures metric; and a decoy rule, "the far side is the farthest point".
why: All four statements held, and all four are known geometry: the half-turn is the cut locus of the circle taken by itself, classical circles of distributions can always be shortcut through the bigger space, and a circle of pure quantum states cannot. CRR adds no prediction here. The leftover is an open question: which families contain a closed curve that is cut exactly at its half-turn?

alternatives.null_worlds: 40 random circles: F1 held on 40, F2 on 40

operating_characteristics: Identity room: every statement is a theorem or its numerical echo, so no outcome weighs for or against CRR as a claim about the world.
second_check: Adapted and re-run by a worker who did not write the mapping. No person has reviewed it.
variants: V-mathematical-1 (cut at the cut locus; torus and sphere numbers; museum experiment, not the owner's CRR)
